races.name: Dandara Homes EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Golwg Gwendraeth Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Our Fella
runners_data.note: Hold-up type representing J S Moore who fires 1 from 14 over the last fortnight; his two runs on Good ground produced a place and a fifth, giving him the most relevant going profile in the field, and his TS from recent runs makes him one to track off a compressed pace.

runners_data.name: Tallahassee Lassie
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan takes the ride for Fanshawe, who is in form at 4/18 over 14 days; her style is genuinely unclassified so she could go forward or stalk, giving her tactical flexibility that is rare in this all-hold-up field and makes her the most adaptable runner.

runners_data.name: Drum Major
runners_data.note: Poor recent form string of 9-7-6-8 with no win or place, though he has shown up on similar Good ground twice; jockey Kavanagh takes a 3lb claim but the horse's overall profile is weak and he is a true closer in a race that may not reward that style.

runners_data.name: Persian Sunset
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy has three winners from 11 runners in the last fortnight; a genuine hold-up runner in form terms, placed last time, but the map has pushed him into midfield because the field is congested with closers — his natural late kick may be neutralised by the slow tempo, tempering confidence in his chance.

runners_data.name: Devon Angel
runners_data.note: Rod Millman sends out a lightly weighted 45-OR two-year-old returning after 63 days, the longest absence in the field; a true closer by inclination, his position on the pace map is a consequence of redistribution rather than his actual racing pattern, and the layoff combined with the lowest rating here makes him a speculative runner at best.

races.paceDynamic: With all five runners carrying a hold-up or unclassified style, this 5f Ffos Las nursery lacks a natural front-runner, meaning the field will likely drift away from the gates in search of a leader before settling into a steady-to-moderate early tempo. Our Fella and Drum Major are the deepest closers in the field, while Tallahassee Lassie's unclassified tag leaves her tactical position genuinely open. The absence of genuine pace means the race will compress into a sprint from roughly halfway, with no horse able to steal a decisive march from the front. This shape strongly favours runners who can travel economically in the pack and produce a sharp, sustained finish over the final two furlongs — a profile that suits horses with a high finishing TS relative to their OR. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can distinguish at the rear: Persian Sunset and Devon Angel are genuine closers shown in midfield due to redistribution, and in a race with no pace injection they are unlikely to benefit from their natural style.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Crawl Then Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field sets a dawdling early tempo and the race ignites only inside the final 2f.
scenarios.body: No horse dominates from the front, so the group compresses before a mass sprint over the last furlong; horses with the cleanest turn of foot and highest TS win from the pack.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Moderate Gallop, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Tallahassee Lassie or a resolute runner elects to go forward and sets an honest but not punishing tempo.
scenarios.body: A runner who claims a prominent pitch without being pressured can control the race and simply quicken away from the field in the final furlong; the honest pace suits a horse with stamina as much as raw speed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Swamp Field
scenarios.trigger: If the early tempo is fractionally more genuine and the closers get a true run through.
scenarios.body: Persian Sunset and Devon Angel, though mapped to midfield, are genuine come-from-behind types and if they get a clean passage on a faster surface they can scythe through; this scenario is discounted because neither is in their natural position and the pace is unlikely to suit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, No Rhythm
scenarios.trigger: If the lack of a pace-maker creates a false start, repeated checking, and a non-run race.
scenarios.body: Horses are shuffled, positions become irrelevant, and the most straightforward traveller who avoids traffic wins; Drum Major's consistency in similar fields gives it relevance here.

watchPoints.text: Watch for Tallahassee Lassie drifting forward at the start — if Rossa Ryan elects to make the running from the gate, she becomes the sole pace-setter and could control the race entirely on her own terms.

Monitor the pace in the opening furlong: if all five runners check and crawl, the final sprint becomes a lottery and draws/barriers could be decisive — any runner drawn widest faces the most ground to make up.

Devon Angel's 63-day absence and lowest OR (45) in the field is a flag — Millman runners returning from breaks need watching for signs of ring-rustiness in the pre-race paddock before treating them as a live factor.

Persian Sunset showed a place last time (3rd, 5f, Soft) which is the most recent form of note in the field — if the ground has any cut remaining at Ffos Las, that run reads better than it looks on paper against this moderate nursery field.

Our Fella's jockey Taylor Fisher rides for a trainer (J S Moore) who has only one winner from 14 runners in the last fortnight — note if Fisher opts to track a prominent position rather than drop in, as that would change Our Fella's profile significantly in a race with no natural leader.

races.name: Preventapest Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Follow Your Heart
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator with five recent runs on good or similar ground producing one win and two places in 15 similar-going starts, but current form reads -46400 suggesting she is out of sorts; George Wood rides and the 30-day break is unremarkable, though at OR 70 she sits at the top of the weights.

runners_data.name: Tokyo Joe
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's four-year-old has winning form over shorter at Sandown and is stepping back to a more prominent role, though the [STYLE_FIT=0.93] flag signals this pace-setting assignment is slightly out of character; Shoemark is a strong booking but the horse's best efforts came at 6f and the step up to 7½f on good at Ffos Las is a new test.

runners_data.name: Freddie's Star
runners_data.note: Roger Teal's charge won over 7f at Sandown last time in hold-up style and has scope to run well fresh after 24 days, though the step back from 8f and a move to Owen Lewis (5lb claimer) are worth noting; similar-going record is a modest 0W0P from 8 runs.

runners_data.name: Mayberry Moon
runners_data.note: Thomas Faulkner's four-year-old has a win over 7f on soft and three places from nine similar-going starts, including a recent fourth on good over 8f just 15 days ago; the hold-up tag is well established and Rossa Ryan, who rides plenty of winners, is an upgrade in the saddle.

runners_data.name: Counting Cards
runners_data.note: Ed de Giles' gelding is a true closer by nature, showing a place finish over 8f at Sandown from the rear, though the field's glut of hold-up types means he is likely to end up racing closer to the pace than ideal; the 57-day break is the longest in the field and form reads 27-490, offering little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Dandy G Boy
runners_data.note: Warren Greatrex's four-year-old has winning and placed form over 7f on good — including a win at Sandown — giving him genuine course-distance profile, though his natural style is hold-up and the overcrowded rear means Edward Greatrex will need to decide early whether to push forward; trainer has had one winner from nine runners in 14 days, quiet but not cold.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of The Bay
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old veteran with ten similar-going runs producing one win and three places, showing consistency across 7-8f on good ground, yet the redistribution reflects that four genuine closers cannot all sit last; Taylor Fisher is a 5lb claimer and the horse carries just 129lbs which helps.

runners_data.name: Redredrobin
runners_data.note: Malcolm Saunders' nine-year-old has placed form at this trip and went second over 7f on soft, showing he stays the distance and goes on cut, but eight runs on good have yielded just one win and two places from 15 similar-going starts; forced to race further forward than his natural position, his finishing kick may be blunted.

runners_data.name: Kaleidoscope Eyes
runners_data.note: Ryan Kavanagh claims 3lbs for Bernard Llewellyn's four-year-old, who has prominent-style form and a win over 8f at Hereford to his name; similar-going figures are underwhelming at 0W0P from 15 runs, but the light weight and a prominent style that suits this race shape make him one of the more interesting tactical options.

races.paceDynamic: Tokyo Joe is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure him, Kieran Shoemark can control the fractions from the front on a flat 7½f Ffos Las track, setting a measured, sustainable gallop that will likely keep the field bunched. The hold-up contingent — Follow Your Heart, Freddie's Star, Mayberry Moon, and the redistributed Counting Cards, Dandy G Boy, Spirit Of The Bay, and Redredrobin — are all competing for the same rear ground, and at a steady pace they will need a strong finishing kick from a compressed position rather than a true sustained run. This field holds substantially more hold-up types than can realistically secure their natural position: Dandy G Boy, Counting Cards, Spirit Of The Bay, and Redredrobin are true rear-end horses mapped to midfield because the back of the race is simply overcrowded, meaning several will end up closer to the pace than they prefer. The tactical verdict is clear: with one uncontested pace-setter on a flat track and a muddled hold-up contingent jostling for position, the race favours horses who can travel prominently just off the leader or race in a handy midfield spot with a clean passage — not the genuine deep closers who face a wall of traffic in an uncompetitive gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tokyo Joe Controls, Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Tokyo Joe is allowed to dictate a comfortable rhythm unchallenged and quickens from the front in the straight.
scenarios.body: Shoemark rolls Tokyo Joe off the pace in a race with no pressure, controlling the tempo until unleashing a front-running burst that the hold-up horses, stuck in a crawl, cannot wind up quickly enough to reel in. Horses that have tracked him handy — Kaleidoscope Eyes and Mayberry Moon — are best placed to strike if Tokyo Joe tires, but Tokyo Joe's [STYLE_FIT] tag suggests he has previously raced differently; if this is genuinely his best shape the odds shorten considerably.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Handy Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Tokyo Joe sets a falsely slow pace that bunches the field and a prominent-handy type swoops off his shoulder in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A compressed field tracking the leader means Mayberry Moon or Dandy G Boy, who despite redistribution have prominent form in their history, are able to sit close enough to strike the moment the pace quickens approaching the furlong marker. The flat Ffos Las straight offers no hiding place and a horse with a clean inside berth and a strong recent run — Mayberry Moon won at 7f on soft and has good-going place form — is ideally suited.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely in the straight, creating a sprint finish where a genuine closer finds a gap late.
scenarios.body: A truly pedestrian gallop that only unravels in the last 150 yards hands an opportunity to a horse with raw finishing speed arriving late through a parting field; Follow Your Heart and Freddie's Star are the truest hold-up operators in the field. However, the overcrowded rear and the redistributed types clogging the midfield make a clean run for a pure closer genuinely difficult, keeping this scenario at low probability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Closers Swamped
scenarios.trigger: If Tokyo Joe surprisingly injects a sharper early tempo that strings the field out and the hold-up horses are left with too much ground to make up.
scenarios.body: An unusually strong gallop from the front would disadvantage the majority of this field who are hold-up types now racing out of position, while any horse who has tracked Tokyo Joe early at a sensible distance would gain most. This scenario is assigned low probability because Tokyo Joe is the only pace horse and has a [STYLE_FIT] flag, and a true strong-pace race is the least likely shape here.

watchPoints.text: Tokyo Joe holds the key to the entire race — if Kieran Shoemark presses forward and controls from the front unchallenged, the odds of a front-running success increase sharply and the hold-up horses may never get into the race.

Dandy G Boy and Counting Cards are being mapped into midfield but are natural hold-up horses; watch where Edward Greatrex and William Cox settle them in the early stages, as a bunched field could see them trapped wide or pocketed with nowhere to go.

Mayberry Moon's jockey Rossa Ryan could choose to push forward off the pace given the horse's prominent-handy placed form — if he does, that is a significant move given the weak gallop set by Tokyo Joe, and the horse's 15-day turnaround shows he is race-fit.

Going is listed as unknown at Ffos Las across all reports; if the ground is softer than good, horses with soft-ground form — Mayberry Moon, Redredrobin — move up in the reckoning, while Tokyo Joe's effectiveness may diminish.

Freddie's Star's trainer Roger Teal has had zero winners from eight runners in the past 14 days — a cold yard flag worth noting when assessing confidence in the horse's chance, despite the positive form line.

races.name: Dandara, Beautiful New Homes In Carway "Confined" Handicap Stakes (For Horses Which Have Not Won A Flat Race In 2026)

runners_data.name: Havana Tobouggaloo
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer whose best recent effort was a second at 8f on soft, but has three runs on good ground without a win and faces a step up to 1m2f that stretches her stamina; Alfie Redman's 7lb claim is an asset but Zoe Hawkins has had a quiet 14-day period at 0/3.

runners_data.name: Racing Demon
runners_data.note: Ed de Giles runner with a solid placed record — four placings from 15 runs on comparable going — and two of his last three efforts at 8f on good ground were competitive; William Cox takes over in the saddle and the 21-day break looks fine for a six-year-old who has held his form.

runners_data.name: Homeland
runners_data.note: Thomas Faulkner's yard is in decent nick at 3/9 over 14 days and this four-year-old has placed twice at 8f on good and soft recently, the step to 1m2f looking a logical progression; Rossa Ryan is a significant jockey booking and the 29-day freshener suits a lightly-raced sort.

runners_data.name: Praise Indeed
runners_data.note: In truth a rear-of-field operator whose natural territory is holding up and finishing late, but with the entire field similarly inclined he is effectively mapped to midfield without that being his comfort zone — four runs at 8f on good ground have yielded nothing, and the style-fit discount of 0.90 is warranted.|

runners_data.name: Gert Lush
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old veteran whose second at 10f on good ground 43 days ago was his most relevant piece of recent form; though placed into midfield on the map, this horse genuinely wants to come from off the pace and Roger Teal's yard is quiet at 0/8 over 14 days, so market confidence would need to be high before elevation.

runners_data.name: Hammal
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish and his last six runs have produced no better than seventh — the redistribution into midfield on the map does not mask the underlying concern that this horse simply finds little under pressure; Max Young's 0/5 in 14 days adds no trainer encouragement and the 13-day turnaround is the shortest in the field.

runners_data.name: Prophet Squeeze
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who has run 7-11-7-6-11 in his last five starts at 8-20f on good and soft — the form reads as a horse in the doldrums — and though he slots into midfield on the map, his natural inclination to race held up means he needs something to go right tactically in a chaotic sprint finish.

runners_data.name: Madame Passant
runners_data.note: The youngest in the field at three, this filly showed a glimpse of ability with a third at 10f on good ground 17 days ago and that recent competitive effort is the best piece of live form in the race at this trip; headgear (h) is noted and Taryn Langley's 5lb claim is useful, though Charlie Pike is at 1/8 in 14 days so the yard is not firing freely.

runners_data.name: Ibiza Lights
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish and fitted with a visor, this three-year-old placed at 10f on good ground on the last occasion but has since run two poor efforts at shorter; George Wood takes over for Michael Bell who has been active at 2/20 in 14 days, and the style-fit note means the midfield map position does not truly represent where this horse wants to race from.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in the field and all nine runners carrying a hold-up profile, this 1m2f contest at Ffos Las is almost certain to be run at a crawling early pace before collapsing into a sprint finish from the home turn. There is no horse likely to force the gallop, meaning the field will bunch through the first mile and the decisive move will come late — favouring whoever can produce the sharpest finish from a compressed pack. The redistribution note is critical here: Praise Indeed, Gert Lush, Madame Passant, Prophet Squeeze, Hammal, and Ibiza Lights are all genuine hold-up horses displaced into midfield on the map because there are simply too many rear-runners for the positions to be authentic. In a truly pace-less race over 1m2f on good turf, the tactical verdict is clear — horses with the best form at this trip on good ground and the cleanest recent evidence of finishing speed will hold the advantage, but the chaotic, compression-style finish means positional luck and a well-timed run from a small field will be decisive, broadly suiting Homeland and Racing Demon who sit at the more reliable end of the form profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish, Best Closer Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls early and the race ignites inside the final 2f as a mass sprint, rewarding the horse with the most potent late kick.
scenarios.body: With no pace to stretch the field, the entire group will hit the turn together and the race becomes a short-distance dash, where a clear head and a sharp jockey move matters enormously; Homeland's recent placed efforts at this trip on good ground and Rossa Ryan's positional awareness make this profile highly relevant.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Slight Injection Splits Field
scenarios.trigger: If one or two runners push forward from early on to fill the vacuum and set a moderate pace, creating a genuine contest of stamina over the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: A modestly-run race at 1m2f on good turf over a fair distance will begin to test stamina as the pace lifts, and horses who have competed creditably over 10-12f on similar ground will be at an advantage; Racing Demon's consistent placed record over both 8f and 10f on good and Racing Demon's trainer Ed de Giles angle support a forward pitch.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow enough that one true hold-up horse times a late run perfectly from the rear to catch the front group flat-footed.
scenarios.body: This is theoretically the natural shape given the field's collective profile, but the REDISTRIBUTED flags mean many supposed closers are not genuine hold-up types and the true rear-runners may lack the finishing thrust on good ground to reel in the compression group; Ibiza Lights has placed at 10f on good ground and Madame Passant has a recent third at that trip, giving them the best credentials here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Outsider Profits
scenarios.trigger: If the bunched field causes interference or a traffic problem in the straight, allowing a less-fancied runner to slip clear on the inner or outer uncontested.
scenarios.body: In a field of nine hold-up types with no leader, gaps and pockets of clear running can appear randomly, and a horse like Gert Lush — who recorded a placed second at 10f on good ground — could benefit from a fortuitous split; Hammal and Prophet Squeeze are longer shots who may stumble into contention if the front runners check each other.

watchPoints.text: Watch for Homeland to be produced with a well-timed challenge by Rossa Ryan in the straight — in a slowly-run race his recent placed form at this trip is the most credible and the jockey booking is the standout of the race.

The entire field sitting off no pace means a traffic problem in the straight is a genuine risk — watch for Madame Passant and Ibiza Lights in particular, both young fillies who may find themselves boxed in as the field compresses into the final 2f.
Hammal and Ibiza Lights are both flagged for fading in the finish — if either is prominent at the furlong pole, expect them to be overhauled quickly as the dash for the line develops.

Gert Lush is the oldest runner at nine and has the longest break at 43 days — watch to see if Owen Lewis (5lb claim) positions him handily enough from early on, which would be out of character but could prove decisive in a race with no natural leader.

Racing Demon's record shows four placed efforts from fifteen runs on comparable going — watch whether William Cox elects to push for a prominent berth early to steal a march on the hold-up pack, which could transform the race shape entirely.

races.name: Dandara, Find Your Perfect New Home Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Caelan
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's five-year-old has genuine course-trip form credentials — two wins at 1m4f-1m6f on good and soft ground — and at OR 67 is the form pick, though 16 days since last run and a weight of 142lbs in a field of closers means he needs the sprint to develop cleanly.

runners_data.name: Bulldog Spirit
runners_data.note: Bernard Llewellyn sends this six-year-old out having won only once in fifteen good-ground starts, and despite being a natural closer, he finds himself in a race where he cannot get to the back of the field as intended — his style-fit compromise of 0.92 means his chance should be tempered accordingly.

runners_data.name: Meet Me In Meraki
runners_data.note: David Evans has found a 10-day change since last run (21 days), and Rossa Ryan is an upgrade in the saddle, but Meet Me In Meraki's recent form string of 467873 and only three placings in fifteen good-going starts makes optimism hard to sustain; a true closer now forced to race in midfield, his chance is meaningfully discounted.

runners_data.name: Liveinthelight
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's three-year-old is the form improver here — a win and a second from her last three starts, all at 10f — and racing off only 131lbs, the lightest in the field, she may naturally slide forward in a race that lacks any horse willing to go on; the step up to 1m4f is the key unknown.

runners_data.name: Grand Pier
runners_data.note: Warren Greatrex's three-year-old is on the drift in trip, stepping from 10f up to 1m4f for the first time, and has no wins in seven career starts; a natural closer squeezed into midfield by redistribution, his style-fit score of 0.90 is the lowest in the race and his chance is most reliant on the race falling apart tactically.

races.paceDynamic: Every runner in this five-horse field carries a hold-up profile, meaning there is no confirmed front-runner and no horse bred to dictate from the front — the pace is likely to be dawdling and tactical before the field collapses into a sprint finish over the final two furlongs. Liveinthelight, the youngest in the field at three and racing off the lightest weight, has recently shown a willingness to race prominently (second and first in her last two wins at 10f) and may find herself shuffled forward simply through circumstance rather than design. Caelan, the highest-rated runner at OR 67, has solid form at this sort of trip on good ground but will be content to race off a slow pace and pounce late. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Bulldog Spirit, Meet Me In Meraki, and Grand Pier are all genuine closers now compressed into the midfield picture with style-fit compromises attached — and the overall dynamic strongly favours the runner who can best identify and exploit the sprint phase, giving a clear edge to any horse with sharp finishing pace over rivals racing partially out of role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Tempo Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field idles through the early and middle stages and the race becomes a flat-out dash from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: With no pace-maker to stretch the field, runners will bunch and the outcome hinges on who produces the sharpest late turn of foot; Liveinthelight's recent winning form over shorter trips at good to soft and good suggests she has the required finishing kick.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one runner — most likely Liveinthelight or Caelan under pressure from the jockey — pushes forward early and steals a march on the hold-up pack.
scenarios.body: A lone leader on a flat track with a slow-run race behind them is notoriously hard to peg back in a small field with no rival to set honest fractions; the prominent position would suit Liveinthelight's recent form profile more than any other runner here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp The Line
scenarios.trigger: If a genuine pace develops unexpectedly and the true hold-up horses Bulldog Spirit and Meet Me In Meraki get a rhythm that brings them into the race late.
scenarios.body: Bulldog Spirit has one win in fifteen tries on good ground so the profile is limited, but a strong gallop would give him and Meet Me In Meraki a rare chance to produce their natural style; both carry the style-fit caveat of being mapped out of role, so this outcome is discounted accordingly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Jockey Tactics Decide
scenarios.trigger: If the race is so slowly run that positional manoeuvring in the straight — rather than raw pace — determines the winner.
scenarios.body: Grand Pier, stepping up in trip with the lightest weight in the field and partnered by Edward Greatrex who knows the horse well, could benefit if a muddling race rewards a quick tactical read in the home straight; his OR 62 and zero wins in seven comparable starts makes this a low-probability outcome.

watchPoints.text: Liveinthelight is the only runner who has won recently and may slide into a lead role by default — watch whether George Wood elects to use her in front early, as that would transform the race shape entirely.

The pace is likely to be dangerously slow with five hold-up horses and no confirmed front-runner — any punter relying on a strong gallop to bring Bulldog Spirit or Meet Me In Meraki into play should be cautious.
Grand Pier's trip up to 1m4f is unproven and he has no wins from seven starts — if the race develops into a stamina test rather than a sprint, his form profile is not encouraging.
Caelan carries 142lbs — the heaviest weight in the field by 4lbs — which could be a meaningful factor if the sprint finish is prolonged rather than a sharp two-furlong dash.

Taylor Fisher takes the ride on Bulldog Spirit for a trainer whose 14-day strike rate is 0/6 — the combination of limited going form, redistribution out of role, and trainer form makes this one to monitor rather than trust.
